origins: This belief often appears when stress piles up: illness, caring for a loved one, money problems, grief, or several crises at once. It can also come from growing up without being allowed to face difficulties, or from being overwhelmed as a child with burdens too heavy for a child to carry. The body’s alarm system then fires quickly, and the thought “I can’t handle this” arrives before we have even tried.
teaches: Scripture does not promise that life will be easy, but it does promise that God will not leave us to carry it alone. God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. He tells His people not to fear, because He will strengthen and uphold them. Paul described being hard pressed but not crushed. Jesus invites the weary to come to Him and find rest. You may not be able to handle this by yourself, but you are not by yourself.
self_statements: This is too much for me.
I can’t cope with one more thing.
Other people could handle this, but not me.
If this goes on, I’ll break.
errors: Imagining the worst possible outcome and assuming I will not survive it.
Predicting that I will fall apart before it happens.
Believing I can’t cope because I feel overwhelmed.
Forgetting the hard things I have already gotten through.
questions: What hard things have I already gotten through?
What is the next small step, not the whole mountain?
Am I trying to handle tomorrow’s problems today?
What does God promise to those who are overwhelmed?
Who can help carry part of this load?
What would I tell a friend in my situation?
truth: This is hard, and I feel overwhelmed. But I have gotten through hard things before, and God has promised to strengthen and uphold me. I don’t have to handle everything at once. I can take the next step, ask for help, and lean on Him.
hw_truths: God will strengthen and help me.
I am hard pressed but not crushed.
I only need to take the next step.
I have survived hard things before.
Jesus gives rest to the weary.
log: Each evening, write one hard moment from the day and how you got through it, even if it was messy.
actions: Write the whole situation at the top of a page. Below it, list the smallest next steps. Do only the first one today.
List three hard things you have already survived. Write how God helped you through each one.
Ask one person for one concrete thing, such as a meal, a ride, or an hour of company.
When you feel overwhelmed, stop, breathe slowly for one minute, and pray Isaiah 41:10 aloud.
tracker: A hard moment I got through
prayer: Lord, this feels like more than I can carry. You promised to strengthen me, help me, and hold me up. Show me the next step, send help where I need it, and give me rest in You. Amen.
